newsitem.title: GERMANY: German building employers must honour deal -court.
newsitem.headline: German building employers must honour deal -court.

text.p: A German court on Wednesday declared null and void a move by construction employers to cancel contracts designed to lift east German wages to levels in the west of the country.
The Wiesbaden industrial tribunal ruled that employers must honour the wage contracts. IG-Bau construction sector trade union filed a complaint last September against the cancellation.
The employers' association Hauptverband der Deutschen Bauindustrie had said in August that east German firms could not fund a previously-agreed pay rise for workers there.
The employers association had said the unprecedented move was a response to an emergency situation after eastern firms had threatened to pull out of existing wage agreements in droves.

The contracts would have put into effect a 1.85 percent wage rise and an agreement that would have pushed average east German construction wages up to 95 percent of west German levels from 92 percent.
A spokesman for IG Bau responded by demanding back-payment and called on employers to discuss future wage policies for east Germany.
